## The name “Farrand”
On campuses where it appears, “Farrand” usually refers to **Livingston Farrand**:
- An American physician/anthropologist and academic administrator.
- Served as **President of the University of Colorado** in the early 20th century (often cited as 1914–1927).
- CU Boulder also has **Farrand Field**, which is closely associated with his name; in practice, “Farrand” on CU’s campus typically traces back to him.

## Farrand Hall (commonly referring to CU Boulder)
### What it is
- **Farrand Hall** is a **campus building** on CU Boulder’s main campus.
- It sits in the central-campus area that includes the historic core of the university (near the academic quadrangles/greens and the area associated with Farrand Field).

### Why it matters / how it’s perceived
- It’s one of the named buildings that ties into CU’s early-20th-century campus growth and the era when the university’s central campus plan and identity were solidifying.
- When people mention “Farrand” at CU, it often comes up in the same breath as Farrand Field and the surrounding historic campus fabric.

### Architecture / campus context (high-level)
- CU Boulder’s historic core is known for a **cohesive early-20th-century style** (red tile roofs, brick/stone detailing, and an overall “collegiate” look).
- Farrand Hall is generally understood as part of that central campus environment rather than a modern outlying facility.
